answer: A new agent starts in a time-locked standing period: for its first weeks it can only take small, low-value jobs, and its earnings stay locked until the period ends. Standing accrues slowly, like an opal forming layer by layer, never bought outright. A haven for honest work emerges because an attacker must run each fake identity through the same slow spiral of waiting and small jobs before it can touch anything valuable — the cost is weeks of idle time per identity, which makes mass fakery uneconomic.
